_notes: The seminary as a house with a rule (seminary depth round). `day` is the horarium as posted, for the sheet. `horarium` are its lines kept at a level: the minimum frees an hour a week and costs piety and the house's regard (rector and vice-rector), the invested level costs an hour and gives back; `visible` lines are the ones the vice-rector's notebook sees. `devotions` are the man's own rule of prayer, kept in his own time before Lauds and after Compline, up to RULE.maxDevotions at once; `strain` is the rest they cost. `recreation` is what he does with the evening hour as a habit: human formation, friends, rest, and `late`, the chance a night runs late enough to miss Lauds. Flags written by the setters: horarium:<key>:<quality>, rule:<id>, recreation:<id>. Numbers invented; the scenes in events/seminary/rule.json read the flags.

day.label: Breakfast, in silence in the propaedeutic year
Classes, the apostolate, or the free hours
The gym, the grounds, the library
Vespers, and a holy hour on Thursdays
Compline, and the Grand Silence after it

blurb.min: Lauds when you wake in time, Compline when you are in. The stall is empty often enough to be noticed.
blurb.standard: Lauds and Vespers with the house, and Compline most nights.
blurb.invested: Every hour, in your stall, the psalms by heart by Lent.

blurb.min: The back pew, and the door, and sometimes neither.
blurb.standard: The house Mass, every morning, and a reading when it is your turn.
blurb.invested: Serving, or in the schola, or the one who sets the sacristy; the Mass as a thing you help make.

horarium.label: Meals and recreation with the house

blurb.min: A sandwich in the room, the tray at the door; the table notices who is not at it.
blurb.standard: The refectory, three times a day, and the hour after supper with whoever is there.
blurb.invested: Every table, the old priests' table on Sundays, the argument carried into the corridor.

horarium.label: The study hall and the Grand Silence
horarium.time: Study 7:30 to 9:00 in the propaedeutic year; silence from 10:00

blurb.min: The phone on, the door open, the corridor at eleven.
blurb.standard: The silence kept, mostly; the phone face down after Compline.
blurb.invested: The silence as a discipline: the phone in the drawer, the room dark at ten, the morning clear.

devotions.label: The rosary
devotions.blurb: Five decades a day, walked in the garden or said in the dark. The oldest habit in the house and the one most men keep after it.

devotions.label: Lectio divina
devotions.blurb: Half an hour with the Sunday Gospel before Lauds: read, read again, say nothing. The homily begins here years before you preach one.
digest: half an hour with Sunday's Gospel

devotions.label: The examen
devotions.blurb: Ten minutes at night over the day as it was. The Jesuits' habit, and the one that makes the file honest.

devotions.label: The Office of Readings
devotions.blurb: The hour the house does not say in common: the Fathers at six in the morning, in your room, with coffee. A priest's habit begun early.
digest: the Office of Readings at six
the Fathers before the house is up

devotions.label: The chapel at night
devotions.blurb: An hour before the tabernacle after Compline, with the key the sacristan lends. Nobody sees it. That is the point, and the cost is the morning.
digest: an hour in the dark before the tabernacle

devotions.label: Spiritual reading
devotions.blurb: Twenty minutes a day in a book that is not on any syllabus: Thérèse, de Caussade, the Cloud. The director will ask what you are reading.

devotions.label: The Friday fast
devotions.blurb: Bread and water on Fridays, through the term. The body learns what the will is for; the refectory learns to leave your plate.
digest: a Friday with an empty plate

recreation.label: The common room
recreation.blurb: Cards, the game on, the argument about the professor that nobody wins. Where the class becomes a class.

recreation.label: The walk
recreation.blurb: Two by two around the grounds after supper, the old seminary custom, and the conversations that happen only walking.
digest: two by two under the trees
the walk, and what was said on it

recreation.label: The music room
recreation.blurb: The piano nobody tunes, a guitar, the men who sing. The schola is born here and so are the house's songs.
digest: the piano in the music room
an hour of the house's songs

recreation.label: The garden
recreation.blurb: The vegetable beds behind the gym that the old Brother keeps, and the men who help him. Dirt, silence, tomatoes in August.
digest: the garden with the old Brother

recreation.label: Thursday film night
recreation.blurb: A film in the lecture hall on Thursdays, chosen by a committee that argues about it all week, and the discussion after that runs past Compline.
digest: the film and the argument after
a film the committee fought over

recreation.label: The phone home
recreation.blurb: The evening hour on the phone to the people who sent you, and the friends who are not here. The house is far away for an hour.
digest: an hour on the phone home

recreation.label: Early to bed
recreation.blurb: The room at nine, the light out at ten, the morning clear. The house thinks you dull. The house is not up at six.
digest: early to bed, and a clear morning

recreation.label: The bar down the hill
recreation.blurb: The standing table at the bar down the hill, two or three nights a week, with the men who go. The class's secrets are kept there, and its drinkers made.
digest: the hill, climbed back after eleven
